source.title: Apollo: An Adaptive Parameter-wise Diagonal Quasi-Newton Method for Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance of SGD and adaptive optimizers across image classification, language modeling, and translation, using optimizer comparisons rather than the original studies’ evaluation setups.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test metrics for its own optimizer comparisons. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, architecture comparisons, dropout effects, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: Independent comparisons of adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD measure held-out performance on new architectures and benchmarks, bearing on V4. Image experiments also test sensitivity to weight-decay tuning. These experiments extend the settings and tuning recipes rather than reproduce the original limited-tuning comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that Apollo improves convergence and held-out performance over the compared optimizers across the three tasks. Their comparisons also show task-dependent SGD versus Adam-family rankings and strong sensitivity to regularization and epsilon.
record.recipe_differences: Optimizer comparisons use different tasks, model architectures, datasets, and tuned training schedules from the original claim’s cited studies; the paper comprehensively tunes hyperparameters, especially learning rate and weight decay, for its image experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome changes by task and optimizer; image-classification results are reported under milestone and cosine learning-rate schedules. AdaBelief’s One Billion Words result is sensitive to epsilon. Weight-decay strength affects optimizer performance.
record.problems: The paper selects successfully converged Adam and RAdam language-model runs and discards runs that crashed due to loss numerical overflow. It reports no uncertainty for the One Billion Words test PPL table. Image experiments are extensively tuned, so they do not directly establish the limited-tuning condition in V4.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results for the other claim versions were reported. The optimizer comparisons in Table 1 duplicate Table 5's more detailed test-accuracy results and were not extracted separately.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

A controlled comparison restricted to learning-rate and schedule tuning on images; tuning also includes weight decay and sometimes epsilon. No controlled demonstration that decoupling weight decay itself recovers performance, no Adam-to-SGD switching, and no systematic test of Adam's advantage on word-level language models. Numerical training-performance comparisons are not captured by the supplied text's figure descriptions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Adam* and RAdam* use SGD's weight-decay rate. CIFAR-10 milestone/cosine accuracies are Adam*: 91.41±0.30/91.56±0.19 and RAdam*: 91.80±0.04/91.88±0.15; ImageNet values are Adam*: 71.72±0.13/71.19±0.10 and RAdam*: 72.37±0.08/71.64±0.14. Compare with the existing SGD baselines and tuned Adam/RAdam rows. These are distinct conditions, not duplicates of Table 1.

The authors explicitly report that adjusting Adam/RAdam weight decay improves accuracy while slowing convergence, and that their initially fast convergence reflects relatively weak regularization. Capture this qualification alongside the starred and tuned conditions.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says momentum SGD was not compared: Section 4 and Appendices D.1/D.3 explicitly specify momentum, including 0.9. Adaptive first-order baselines use decoupled weight decay wherever weight decay is applied. Table 5's surrounding text identifies the reported image uncertainty as standard deviations over five runs, despite the caption's wording. Small numerical differences are not treated as proven statistically significant effects.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.

The paper does not compare against momentum SGD on the specified benchmarks, does not test the broader tuning of Choi et al., and does not test switching from Adam to SGD. Its language-model experiment is word-level, but does not establish the version’s wider language-benchmark claim.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout comparisons and removal of dropout or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.
